derived_results.claim: Split misalignment can be handled exactly at the r68 conditional-SNML identity level without pretending a contaminated scored segment is generated by one Gaussian.
derived_results.statement: For candidate s with total pre length T=s and evaluated post length H, define U=X_1:b, A=X_{b+1:s}, V=X_{s+1:s+b}, B=X_{s+b+1:s+H}. Pathwise, log C=[lhat(U∪A)-lhat(U)-r_b(T)]+[lhat(V∪B)-lhat(V)-r_b(H)]-lhat(A∪B), regardless of where the true changepoint lies. For any block formed from homogeneous Gaussian subgroups h, sample subgroup means M_h=mu_h+sigma_h Z_h/sqrt(n_h) and within sums W_h=sigma_h^2 ChiSq_{n_h-1}, mutually independently; aggregate mean is sum n_h M_h/N and aggregate SSE is sum W_h+sum n_h(M_h-M)^2. These elementary variables generate every lhat term exactly and preserve all covariance between contaminated SSE and means.
derived_results.early_neighbor_groups: If the true change is x observations after the early candidate: U=P^b; A=P^(T-b); V=P^min(x,b) Q^(b-min(x,b)); B=P^(x-b)_+ Q^(H-b-(x-b)_+).
derived_results.late_neighbor_groups: For the next candidate g-x observations after the true change, with T'=T+g: U=P^b; A=P^(T'-b-(g-x)) Q^(g-x); V=Q^b; B=Q^(H-b).
derived_results.consequence: The r71 rectangular/GLR-overfit route is not the right object for misalignment: a contaminated scored segment is not one true Gaussian R, so homogeneous-block D_R arguments cannot simply be reused. The exact conditional-SNML identity avoids that mismatch.

derived_results.claim: A pair-power certificate can use marginal candidate failure bounds without modeling early/late dependence.
derived_results.statement: Let F_e and F_l be the events that the weighted early and late candidates respectively fail their own global-PFA crossing thresholds. Failure of the pair max implies F_e∩F_l, hence P(pair fails)<=min(P(F_e),P(F_l)). Therefore for each fixed Q and offset x it is enough to upper-bound both marginal failure probabilities and keep the smaller valid upper bound; no independence assumption between neighboring candidates is required.

derived_results.claim: The exact conditional-SNML misalignment simulator supports a much smaller 10-individualized-state three-scale bank on a dense finite parameter grid, with simultaneous exact-binomial uncertainty accounting.
derived_results.certification_grid: For each scale, 15 log-spaced variance ratios spanning the complete normalized Gaussian KL=I level and 17 evenly spaced changepoint offsets x∈[0,g] were checked: 765 (Q,x) points. At each point, 4000 exact sufficient-statistic draws were run for each neighbor. One-sided Clopper-Pearson upper limits used per-test delta=0.001/(2*765), so by a union bound all 1530 marginal upper limits cover simultaneously with confidence at least 0.999 over the offline simulation randomness.
derived_results.comparison: This reduces individualized split state from the r71 lead 27 to 10 (about 63% reduction), and from the older r69 bank 52 to 10 (about 81% reduction), while retaining the same three future-tail states.
derived_results.scope: This is a rigorous randomized certificate only on the finite scanned grid, conditional on the exact simulator/identity; Clopper-Pearson controls Monte Carlo uncertainty but does not certify unsampled points between KL/offset grid values. It is not yet an adoption-grade continuum theorem.

derived_results.claim: A denser independent engineering scan did not reveal an interior failure spike for the 10-state design.
derived_results.details: Using 21 log-spaced KL-level variance ratios and 33 offsets per scale (2079 parameter points), 1500 exact draws per neighbor, the largest empirical min-neighbor threshold-failure rates were 0.0267 for I=1, 0.0580 for I=0.5 and 0.0313 for I=0.25. This has no simultaneous confidence claim and is only a gap-finding stress test.

candidates_new.mechanism: Certify split mismatch directly from the exact conditional-SNML pathwise identity and subgroup sufficient statistics, rather than degrading a homogeneous two-sample GLR certificate.
candidates_new.confidence: high for the exact representation and pair-failure inequality; medium-high for the finite-grid design evidence.

candidates_new.mechanism: Use {T0,g,H}={(256,16,64),(500,32,96),(1024,64,192)} with b=16 and fixed PFA weights, for 10 individualized states plus 3 future tails.
candidates_new.confidence: medium; strong finite-grid randomized evidence but no continuum guarantee yet.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Extend the r71 homogeneous-block D_R/GLR certificate directly to contaminated segments.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected as stated. The contaminated scored block is not generated by one Gaussian member R, so the homogeneous MLE-overfit decomposition is not automatically valid. Use the exact r68 candidate identity instead.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: The previous 27-state lead is close to the minimum state needed.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected by finite-grid exact-simulator evidence. Ten individualized states are enough on all 765 certified grid points, with worst simultaneous marginal-pair failure upper bound below 0.073.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: The 10-state design is already continuum-certified over every Gaussian Q with KL>=the floor and every real-valued offset.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not established. The current confidence accounting is exact only for simulator Monte Carlo at a finite grid; between-grid parameter coverage remains the main proof gap.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: A 10-state design with the weak scale H=160 is comfortably certified.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected under simultaneous grid uncertainty accounting. At I=0.25, H=160 produced a worst grid min-neighbor Clopper-Pearson upper bound about 0.1031, just above beta=0.10. Increasing H to 192 costs no extra individualized state because ceil(192/64)=3 and reduces the worst strict upper bound to about 0.0466.

frontier: Convert the finite KL/offset grid into a continuum certificate. The cleanest route is interval subdivision over variance-ratio r and offset x with conservative envelopes for subgroup sufficient-statistic distributions/log C, or a Lipschitz/stochastic-order argument that makes the endpoint/grid coverage rigorous.

Investigate whether the exact conditional-SNML log-C lower tail along a fixed Gaussian KL level is also worst at a variance endpoint after misalignment; r70 proved this only for population GLR and r71/r72 provide numerical evidence, not a finite-sample theorem.
Use the same exact subgroup representation to derive deterministic or interval-arithmetic bounds on threshold-failure probability, replacing randomized grid certification where practical.

Explore a 9-state design by trading later deterministic activation T0 for shorter H on one scale; do not reduce H alone because the 10-state design is already near the beta boundary on some finite-grid cases.

Compare the separable candidate-wise null-infimum objective against the shared-null infimum-after-sum detector under the exact same small-state schedule so memory optimization is not tuned to a materially weaker detector.
Do not generalize the Gaussian subgroup certificate to heavy tails or non-Gaussian alternatives without a separately valid robust class.
exact_next_action: Build a continuum-safe envelope for the 10-state design over each rectangle in (log variance ratio r, changepoint offset x). Start with the I=0.5 scale because it has the largest simultaneous grid failure upper bound (~0.0727). Bound how each subgroup normal mean and within-SSE law changes across a small parameter cell, propagate that through the exact r68 log-C identity, and certify min{p_fail_early,p_fail_late}<0.10 on the whole cell. If direct stochastic envelopes are too loose, use interval subdivision plus conservative coupling/importance bounds. In parallel test a 9-state activation-vs-lifetime trade only after preserving a nontrivial beta margin.
